note.text: Road development includes route planning, construction, drainage, surfacing and maintenance. Terrain, rainfall, finance, settlement and demand affect what is feasible. A road can provide flexible access to dispersed settlements, but a map line alone does not show its seasonal condition. Drainage and maintenance can be as important as initial construction.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain a road-development factor and calculate a model journey time. Builds on: network links and access. Leads to: rail transport and economic impacts.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Road development includes route planning, construction, drainage, surfacing and maintenance. Terrain, rainfall, finance, settlement and demand affect what is feasible. A road can provide flexible access to dispersed settlements, but a map line alone does not show its seasonal condition. Drainage and maintenance can be as important as initial construction.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented upland case near Bamenda, rain damages a poorly drained access road. Repairing the surface without drainage may give only temporary improvement. For arithmetic practice, a fictional vehicle travels {60} km at a constant model speed of {30} km per hour: time is {60/30} hours or {60/30*60} minutes. This is not a real journey estimate or speed recommendation.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Connect the factor to the engineering or access problem. In calculations divide distance by speed, then convert hours to minutes. State the constant-speed assumption; real delays, stops and road conditions change travel time.
